text.p: AptarGroup Inc said Thursday it expected its European operations to see weakness in the fourth quarter do to weak demand in fragrance and cosmetic pumps.

"While it is difficult to predict the timing of the recovery of sales to the fragrance/cosmetics market, we expect the softness that we have experienced in the first nine months of 1996 to continue at least through the fourth quarter," chief executive officer Carl Siebel said in a news release.

"We are optimistic about the viability of sales to the fragrance/cosmetic market over the longer-term, as our products continue to be specified on the majority of new mid and upscale fragrance introductions," Seibel said. "Additionally, we intend to build on the success of our sales growth to the pharmaceutical and personal care markets."
Earlier, the pump and aerosol valve maker reported net income of $9.0 million, or $0.50 a share in the third quarter, compared to $8.5 million, or $0.47 a share a year ago.
